_about: Real Voices (RULES.md §18). All texts were published before 1929, so they're public domain in the US. 'trigger' says when the quote appears. A quote shows once per game, as an italic line under the newspaper or on the event pop-up. 'note' is shown in smaller text under the quote.

quotes.text: The lamps are going out all over Europe; we shall not see them lit again in our lifetime.
quotes.who: Sir Edward Grey, British Foreign Secretary
quotes.note: Recalled in his memoir Twenty-Five Years (1925).
Over a million men volunteered for Kitchener's New Armies.

quotes.text: If I should die, think only this of me: / That there's some corner of a foreign field / That is for ever England.
quotes.note: Brooke died of sepsis on his way to Gallipoli, 23 April 1915.

quotes.text: In Flanders fields the poppies blow / Between the crosses, row on row,
quotes.note: Written near Ypres after the death of a friend.

quotes.text: Patriotism is not enough. I must have no hatred or bitterness towards anyone.
quotes.when: the night before her execution, 11 October 1915

quotes.text: Courage! On les aura! (Courage! We'll get them!)
quotes.who: General Philippe Pétain, order of the day at Verdun

quotes.text: Ils ne passeront pas! (They shall not pass!)
quotes.who: Rallying cry of the defence of Verdun
quotes.note: Linked to General Nivelle's order of 23 June 1916.

quotes.text: I have a rendezvous with Death / At some disputed barricade,
quotes.who: Alan Seeger, American volunteer in the French Foreign Legion
quotes.note: Seeger was killed on the Somme on 4 July 1916.

quotes.text: The darkness crumbles away. / It is the same old druid Time as ever,
quotes.who: Isaac Rosenberg, 'Break of Day in the Trenches'

quotes.text: The world must be made safe for democracy.
quotes.who: President Woodrow Wilson, asking Congress to declare war
Colonel Charles E. Stanton, at Lafayette's tomb in Paris
quotes.note: Often credited to Pershing, who said the words were Stanton's.

quotes.text: 'Good-morning, good-morning!' the General said / When we met him last week on our way to the line.
Bent double, like old beggars under sacks, / Knock-kneed, coughing like hags, we cursed through sludge,
What passing-bells for these who die as cattle? / Only the monstrous anger of the guns.
quotes.note: Owen was killed one week before the Armistice.

quotes.text: Move him into the sun— / Gently its touch awoke him once,
Home policy: I wage war. Foreign policy: I still wage war. Always, I wage war. (Politique intérieure, je fais la guerre; politique extérieure, je fais toujours la guerre.)
quotes.who: Georges Clemenceau, French Prime Minister, to the Chamber of Deputies

quotes.text: With our backs to the wall and believing in the justice of our cause each one of us must fight on to the end.
quotes.who: Field Marshal Sir Douglas Haig, Special Order of the Day

quotes.text: August 8th was the black day of the German Army in the history of this war.
quotes.who: General Erich Ludendorff, My War Memories
